reductions.label: Focal length
reductions.definition: Estimate focal length from a GeoProbe image; error is mean absolute percentage error.

reductions.label: Depth
reductions.definition: Estimate depth in GeoProbe; error is mean absolute relative error, expressed as a percentage.

reductions.label: Object size
reductions.definition: Estimate physical object size; error is mean absolute percentage error.

reductions.label: Ref. height
reductions.definition: Estimate target height using a reference object of known size; error is mean absolute percentage error.

reductions.label: Height ratio
reductions.definition: Estimate the target-to-reference height ratio; error is mean absolute percentage error.

reductions.label: InFlux focal
reductions.definition: Estimate focal length on InFlux photographs; error is mean absolute percentage error.

motion.label: Fixed camera
motion.definition: Object displacement with a fixed camera in Blender.

motion.label: Small shift
motion.definition: Object displacement with a small camera-view change in Blender.

motion.label: Large shift
motion.definition: Object displacement with a large camera-view change in Blender.

a.label: Left/right
a.title: Image-relative left/right
a.definition: Identify whether one object lies to the left or right of another in the supplied view.
a.exampleQuestion: Is the cooking spoon with green heads to the right of the gray whisk? Your response should be a single word: yes or no.

a.label: Relations
a.title: Object relations
a.definition: Infer the spatial relation between objects across the supplied MindCube views.
a.exampleQuestion: Based on these four images (image 1, 2, 3, and 4) showing the green ball from different viewpoints (front, left, back, and right), with each camera aligned with room walls and partially capturing the surroundings: From the viewpoint presented in image 1, what is to the left of the green ball? A. Wall B. Cardboard-covered sliding door C. Window D. Smoking machine

a.label: Shift
a.title: Camera shift
a.definition: Infer how the camera moves between views of the same scene.
a.exampleQuestion: Based on these two views showing the same scene: in which direction did I move from the first view to the second view? A. Directly left B. Diagonally forward and left C. Directly right D. Diagonally forward and right

a.label: Actor
a.title: Actor-relative left/right
a.definition: Judge left and right from the depicted person’s own orientation, rather than the image frame.
a.exampleQuestion: Consider the real-world 3D locations and orientations of the objects. If I stand at the man's position facing where it is facing, is the skateboard on the left or right of me?

a.label: Facing
a.title: Object-facing side
a.definition: Identify which side of an object—front, back, left, or right—faces another specified object.
a.exampleQuestion: Consider the real-world 3D locations and orientations of the objects. Which side of the person on bicycle is facing the "Santa Cruz County Bank" sign?

a.label: Hard
a.title: Four-way video directions
a.definition: From a video, imagine standing beside one object and facing a second. Locate a third object in the front-left, front-right, back-left, or back-right quadrant.
a.exampleQuestion:
If I am standing by the tv and facing the stove, is the refrigerator to my front-left, front-right, back-left, or back-right?
The directions refer to the quadrants of a Cartesian plane (if I am standing at the origin and facing along the positive y-axis).

b.label: Near
b.title: Closer depth
b.definition: Choose the object that is closer to the camera in BOP-ASK.
b.exampleQuestion: Is the cooking spoon with green heads closer to the camera than the whisk with a black handle and yellow wires? Your response should be a single word: yes or no.

b.label: Far
b.title: Farther depth
b.definition: Choose the object that is farther from the camera in BOP-ASK.
b.exampleQuestion: Is the teal colored cooking spoon farther from the camera than the turquoise colored rounded colander? Your response should be a single word: yes or no.

b.label: Camera
b.title: Camera-relative depth
b.definition: Compare objects by their distance to the camera in 3DSRBench.
b.exampleQuestion: Consider the real-world 3D location of the objects. Which object is further away from the camera?

b.label: Object
b.title: Inter-object proximity
b.definition: Identify which object is closer to a specified reference object in 3DSRBench.
b.exampleQuestion: Consider the real-world 3D locations of the objects. Which is closer to the tv, the wooden table or the orange chair?

b.label: Relative
b.title: Relative distance
b.definition: Choose the nearest object to a reference object in a video scene, measuring between their closest points.
b.exampleQuestion: Measuring from the closest point of each object, which of these objects (chair, tv, sofa, stool) is the closest to the dishwasher?

spatial.aggregation: Equal-weight run mean; five runs except Fable (three). Invalid outputs count as unsuccessful on fixed task IDs.

sourceInfo.label: 3DSRBench
sourceInfo.definition: Spatial relations and imagined viewpoints in static images.

sourceInfo.label: MindCube
sourceInfo.definition: Spatial inference across multiple views of a scene.

sources.label: UMD
sources.definition: Functional regions on tools: localize the part that supports the requested action.

sources.label: ReasonAff
sources.definition: Reason about action-conditioned target regions in interaction scenes.

manipulation.scope: All ten CALVIN sequences for all ten models: 100 adopted single-run episodes. Prefixes and full-sequence success reproduce the retained CALVIN results.
manipulation.definition: An execution-error episode contains a failed code-execution round, excluding transport failures, timeouts, and budget guards. Resumed execution requires a later execution_ok=true round. Recovered completion requires a later native-success round.

humanclawQwenRefresh.selection: Latest per-case worker result; not best outcome. Native success flags; all assigned cases retained.
